todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.

validation.evidence: 39 tests, 0 failures. The deterministic interleaving test commits a stale root after removal and before MemberFollowCleanupRecorded while Message, conversation-access, and conversation-follow projectors are stopped; cleanup remains unacknowledged until they cross the Messaging checkpoint, then discovers the root and clears its sender follow. Shared-access coverage proves one retained idempotent cutoff, no unrelated cutoff, ordinary-unfollow cutoff preservation, delayed manual and real reply-auto rejection, and a genuinely newer post-re-add follow.

80 tests, 0 failures. Aggregate coverage proves explicit equal-generation retention records a durable cutoff, ordinary unfollow preserves it, delayed work at or below the cutoff is rejected, historic absent-field events replay, and newer follows remain allowed; existing message, reply, projection, access-union, and send behavior also passes.
All changed Elixir source and test files are formatted.

notes: Shared conversations now dispatch the existing idempotent UnfollowConversation cleanup with retain_follow=true, producing ConversationUnfollowed(follow_retained=true) so ConversationFollowers durably records the removed-group generation while preserving effective access through another group; aggregate apply honors explicit retention even at an equal generation, and ordinary unfollow leaves cleanup generations/completed IDs intact. RecordMemberFollowCleanup is internally requested as an ExecutionResult and the global durable checkpoint read immediately after dispatch is combined with the originating checkpoint, so both new-event and event-free exact-retry paths wait Message, conversation-access, and conversation-follow projectors through a point at or after MemberFollowCleanupRecorded before enumeration. Historic events default follow_retained to false and existing generation comparison still preserves older-cleanup/newer-follow replay behavior. Accepted task-001 removal semantics remain covered by the focused dispatch suites: transitions emit only GroupMemberRemoved, exact retry emits no Membership fact, and club roles/membership plus system-group guards remain unchanged. Superseded TDD runs first failed on the missing retain_follow field, then exposed an invalid empty-recipient fixture and the need for one :all transient Messaging subscription; the corrected focused suites pass.
